Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

say hello to … for me phrase

also say hello, give my regards, says hello to you, sends greetings, sends her regards, give my love to, give him my best regards, give her my best regards, best regards, send my regards

classical

Traupman 17
Cic. Att. 4.14.2, cited by L&S: Dionysium jubē salvēre

Jubē Mārcum salvēre.

say hello to Marcus for me

Other words

  • salūtem dīcere (alicui) — send greetings, say hello (from someone)

    salūtem, accusative of salūs, with dīcere and the dative of the person greeted · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 14.19.6: tū Atticae salūtem dīcēs (Lewis & Short), s.v. salūs; Cic. Fam. 14.7.3: salūtem plūrimam dīcit (Lewis & Short); Traupman 100

    The opening of a Roman letter, S. D. (salūtem dīcit), and the way to pass on someone’s greetings: Terentia tibi salūtem dīcit.

  • multam salūtem dīcere (alicui) — send someone one’s warmest greetings

    also used · classical · Plaut. Poen. 1.2.194: multam salūtem dīcere alicui, to greet heartily (Lewis & Short s.v. multus); Cic. Att. 2.12.4: Terentia impertit tibi multam salūtem (Lewis & Short s.v. impertiō); Traupman 106: give him (her) my best regards, dīcitō eī multam meīs verbīs salūtem

    Meīs verbīs, “in my words”, is “from me”: Piliam meīs verbīs cōnsōlēre (Cic. Att. 5.11.7, Lewis & Short s.v. cōnsōlor).

Examples

  • Jubē aviam salvēre!

    Say hello to Grandma for me!composed

  • Terentia tibi salūtem dīcit.

    Terentia says hello to you.Traupman 100

  • Atticae, quoniam, quod optimum in puerīs est, hilarula est, meīs verbīs suāvium dēs volō.

    Give Attica a kiss from me, since she is cheerful, the best thing in children.Cic. Att. 16.11.8

  • Dīcitō eī multam meīs verbīs salūtem.

    Give him my best regards.Traupman 106

See also how are you?, goodbye.
